verdict: Digital Realty's revenue jumped 21% to $1.9B as data-center rent rose 17% and utility pass-throughs surged, though $539M of depreciation kept GAAP profit at $0.48 a share while cash-style Core FFO reached $2.10.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $1,902M, vs $1,577M a year ago

kpis.label: Core FFO per share
kpis.note: vs $1.89 a year ago — the cash-earnings measure REIT investors watch, because it adds back depreciation

kpis.label: Fee income
kpis.note: Up 107% YoY — fees for managing and developing data centers for partners

segments.name: Rental revenues
segments.note: Rent from data-center space — the core business. Up 17% as new capacity leased up and rents rose.

segments.name: Tenant reimbursements — utilities
segments.note: Tenants repaying Digital Realty for the electricity their servers use — a pass-through that grows with power-hungry AI workloads.

segments.name: Interconnection & other
segments.note: Fees for connecting customers to each other and to cloud networks inside the data centers, plus other services.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.note: Fees for developing and managing data centers owned with partners — more than doubled YoY.

segments.name: Tenant reimbursements — other
segments.note: Tenants repaying other building costs, such as maintenance and services.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — executives, finance, legal and IT. Up from $140M a year ago as the company grows.

opex.name: Transaction & integration
opex.note: Deal costs — buying properties and companies and folding them in. Down from $87M a year ago; Digital Realty treats these as non-core in Core FFO (see one-time items).

opex.name: Severance & legal
opex.note: Severance, equity acceleration and legal expenses — small this quarter.

otherDetail: An $8M gain on selling properties, plus $12M of interest and other income, less an $18M loss from joint-venture data centers, $94M of interest expense, $10M of preferred-stock dividends and a $2M add-back for partners' share of losses — a net $100M cost. The result is the $185M of net income available to common stockholders (total net income before those shareholder-level items was $194M).
follow100Note: Kept-as-profit is the $185M available to common stockholders; the rows add to $100.01 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Rent and power pass-throughs surged
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose 21% to $1,902M. Base rent grew 17% to $1,225M, and tenants' electricity reimbursements jumped 27% to $424M — a direct read on how power-hungry AI data centers have become.

takeaways.title: Cash earnings tell a richer story
takeaways.text: Core FFO — funds from operations, the REIT cash-earnings measure that adds back depreciation — was $2.10 a share, up 11% from $1.89. GAAP EPS was only $0.48 because $539M of depreciation on buildings and equipment is a real accounting cost but not a cash one.

takeaways.title: Deal costs are still a drag
takeaways.text: Transaction and integration costs were $49M in the quarter (down from $87M a year ago), plus $3M of severance and legal costs. Core FFO excludes these, which is part of the gap between the $2.10 Core FFO figure and $0.48 of GAAP EPS.

oneTimers: Transaction and integration expenses of $49M in the quarter ($103M in the first nine months) — costs of acquiring and integrating properties and businesses; Digital Realty excludes them from Core FFO.
An $8M net gain on sales of properties sits in other income, below operating profit.
footerNote: REIT presentation: cost of revenue combines utilities ($478M), rental property operating costs ($304M), insurance ($5M), real estate taxes ($60M) and depreciation & amortization ($539M). Operating income here is before the $8M gain on property sales, which is shown in other income. Figures are rounded to $M; general & administrative absorbs a $1M rounding difference and interest expense a $1M rounding absorption so the lines add exactly.
